cells.tense: The directed work has reached its full form, and what comes next can be met from here.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: When something new arrives this week, take your own part of it, all of it, and leave the rest where it sits.
cells.core:
What you aimed your attention at has reached a standing form, and the way you meet this doorway comes from how it was made. Not from luck — from putting your own weight on your own legs, session after session, until the form held. A threshold feels different when that's true, and what arrives can be taken up from something already tested and proved.

The risk is in how far you reach. Take your own part of what's coming, all of it, and don't stretch past your own arm for the rest. What you carry that way lasts. What you lift that isn't yours is what starts to bend the grip you earned, and nothing arriving here needs that from you.
cells.sheetLine: The work stands. Meet what arrives holding your own share.
cells.verb: finishing what the whole self was pointed at, until it stands
cells.place: the threshold where what is outside is arriving and can be met

cells.tense: You are already braced against something that has not yet arrived to be braced against.
cells.ask: Sit somewhere this week with no task and let whatever comes reach you before you decide what it is.
cells.core:
Something is on its way in, and you have already met it. The next move is decided, the next shape is planned, and your whole weight leans into a door nothing has knocked on. From inside, that reads as readiness. It's running well ahead of what is actually here, and the part of you that could take in something unplanned isn't getting room.

Sit somewhere with no task and stay a while. Let whatever shows come to you, without sorting it or deciding what it is. You already stand well — that part is not in question. The other half is letting what comes reach you before you go out to meet it.

cells.tense: The cycle closed behind you, and your attention is still parked at the edge of a room you already left.
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Write five plain lines about what sits right where you are — what is there, not what it means — and stop at five.
cells.core:
A whole structure got finished, and your attention didn't walk through with it. Everything you made is standing out in your life, and you are meeting the present from the far side of that. What arrives lands dimmer than it is, and nothing in you is choosing from here. You went quiet in the middle of something that was supposed to be yours to stand in.

Sight brings the current back, and sight asks nothing of you yet. Write five plain lines about what is right where you are. What is there, not what it means. Stop at five. Looking accurately, once, is the whole beginning — no finishing, no push, nothing else asked.

cells.tense: The finishing hand was yours, and your own account of it leaves your hand out.
cells.act: notice what is before your eyes before naming it
cells.ask: Next time you explain why something in your life worked, look at what's there before the explanation arrives.
cells.core:
Something you made is standing, and by your own telling it simply appeared. The months were busy, the timing lined up, people helped — all true, none of it the whole. The hand that did the finishing is still in the picture and just doesn't sign. That doing is yours whether or not the credit lands, and the credit is the only part you're withholding from yourself.

The shift is smaller than a claim. Next time you explain why something in your life worked, hold a second before the label. In that second, see what's there before the explanation arrives. You don't have to announce anything, or take a bow, or say it differently to anyone. You only have to not decide what it was before you look. Nothing grows from you standing outside your own work.
cells.sheetLine: You're not claiming the thing you clearly finished.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a material cycle has already completed and something is arriving — the record gives the signature's shape but nothing about this person's actual history, so the cells say only what the capacity is doing, never what happened. A reader could reasonably say 'no, nothing feels finished and nothing feels incoming,' so every cell has to be usable as a description of a posture rather than a verdict about their life. The asks survive that: each one is a small act the person can do this week whether or not the read lands. The sentence that serves the writer is the one that would admire the standing structure — 'look what you built' — and it's cut from all four; what stays is where the capacity sits in the doorway, not a verdict on what's on the other side.
